local_facts.title: Florida sets the shade by the window, not by the car
local_facts.claim: Florida Statutes 316.2953 requires film on the side windows beside and ahead of the driver to pass at least 28 percent of visible light and reflect no more than 25 percent. Section 316.2954 sets the windows behind the driver at 15 percent minimum transmittance and 35 percent maximum reflectance, or 6 percent on multipurpose passenger vehicles such as SUVs and vans. Section 316.2955 allows 3 percent either way on a reading and requires a compliance label inside the driver's door jamb.
local_facts.why_it_matters: The same 20 percent film is legal on a sedan's back glass and illegal on its front doors. Ask for the meter reading on the front glass and check the door-jamb label before driving off.

local_facts.title: A $6.50 certificate covers darker film for a medical reason
local_facts.claim: Section 316.29545 has the Department of Highway Safety and Motor Vehicles issue exemption certificates for lupus, autoimmune disease or other conditions requiring limited light exposure. Form HSMV 83390, revised July 2025, needs a certification from a qualifying physician, PA or nurse practitioner and a copy of a Florida license or ID, mailed to the Bureau of Motorist Compliance. The fee is $6.50 per vehicle; the certificate never expires but is void once the vehicle is sold.
local_facts.why_it_matters: Film darker than the statute allows, or on the windshield below the AS-1 line, is lawful only with this certificate for that exact car, so it should be in hand before the film goes on.

local_facts.title: Milton gusted past 100 mph at the Sarasota-Bradenton airport
local_facts.claim: Hurricane Milton made landfall on the west-central Florida coast as a Category 3 on 9 October 2024. The National Weather Service Tampa Bay report lists Sarasota/Bradenton International Airport at 60 knots sustained with an 89-knot gust, the highest land gust in its table; the National Hurricane Center's 10 p.m. update put it at 102 mph. Florida Statutes 553.842(5) bars marketing any product as hurricane or impact protection without state product approval.
local_facts.why_it_matters: Safety film holds broken glass together, but it is no substitute for shutters or impact windows. A quote calling film hurricane protection without a Florida approval number is a claim the seller may not make.

local_facts.title: One hundred and ten days of 90-degree normal highs
local_facts.claim: The National Weather Service's 1991-2020 daily normals for the Bradenton 5 ESE station put the normal high at 90 degrees or above every day from 31 May through 17 September, 110 days in a row, peaking at 92.0 in July and early August. The station logs 3,773 cooling degree days a year against 438 heating degree days.
local_facts.why_it_matters: A car parked all afternoon and a west-facing slider in Palma Sola take that load for a third of the year. Heat rejection, not darkness, is the number worth comparing.
